what_this_is: Which later work orders moved a market out from under a CONSUMED historical deployment authorization. An authorization is immutable evidence of what was authorized and deployed at the time; later legitimate source growth must NOT make its historical hash read as corrupt. So a test that re-verifies a historical authorization skips exactly the markets named here -- named, never blanket -- and still binds every market that was not moved. A market may only be listed with the work order that moved it.

ptf-auth-indianapolis-006-4d684ebfc742.note: Historical. It was the live authorization until PTF-PITTSBURGH-DEPLOYMENT-AUTHORIZATION-003 shipped Pittsburgh as deploy 6a9c3a1422ead7c0c01b3468. Pittsburgh had moved out from under it in source before that deploy and is named above, so re-verifying this authorization skips exactly that market and still binds every other one.

Nothing moved out from under it while it was live: it was authorized against exactly the source that deployed, and the Toledo promotion that followed changed no byte of the bundle it served, because a non-participating market moves no byte of the composed bundle.

ptf-auth-toledo-003-895248738c79.note: The current live authorization. It admitted toledo-oh as the eleventh market at 17 profiles and moved no other market, and the bundle it binds is the bundle production serves. PTF-DETROIT-ANN-ARBOR-LAUNCH-PREP-031 then moved detroit-ann-arbor-mi out from under it in SOURCE by proposing the market for launch, so a fresh assembly now composes twelve markets while this authorization binds eleven. That is source running ahead of production, not corruption: re-verifying this authorization skips exactly Detroit and still binds every one of the eleven markets it actually authorized, none of which moved. Nothing was deployed and no new authorization exists.
